:::{#exm-cross-entropy-decomposition}
#### Cross-entropy, entropy and divergence for a uniform code

<!-- no-figure: the example is three numbers -->

Let $p = (1/2, 1/4, 1/4)$ be the mass function of a three-valued random variable,
and let $q = (1/3, 1/3, 1/3)$ be the uniform mass function.
The code below computes the cross-entropy, the entropy and the divergence in bits.

```{r}
#| label: cross-entropy-decomposition
p <- c(1 / 2, 1 / 4, 1 / 4)
q <- rep(1 / 3, 3)
cross_entropy <- -sum(p * log2(q))
shannon_entropy <- -sum(p * log2(p))
divergence <- sum(p * log2(p / q))
c(
  cross_entropy = cross_entropy,
  shannon_entropy = shannon_entropy,
  divergence = divergence
)
```

The cross-entropy is $H_2(p, q) = `r round(cross_entropy, 3)`$ bits.
The entropy is $H_2(p) = `r shannon_entropy`$ bits,
and the divergence is $D_2(p \,\|\, q) = `r round(divergence, 3)`$ bits.
They satisfy @thm-cross-entropy-decomposition:
`r shannon_entropy` + `r round(divergence, 3)` = `r round(cross_entropy, 3)`.

:::
